title: Reproductive system and embryonic development
summary: Learn the reproductive organs, the cycle and how the embryo develops, from gamete formation to birth.
cards.0.p: Sperm are made in the testes. The testes sit in a pouch that is 2-3 °C cooler than the body. Sperm mature in the epididymis and are carried by the vas deferens. Mixed with gland secretions, they form semen.
cards.0.key: These glands are the seminal vesicles, the prostate and the bulbourethral glands. In males, the urethra carries both urine and semen.
cards.1.p: Sperm are made in the seminiferous tubules. Sertoli cells are stimulated by FSH and nourish the sperm. Leydig cells are stimulated by LH and secrete testosterone.
cards.1.key: Testosterone keeps sperm production going and causes traits like facial hair and muscle. Testosterone taken from outside (doping) suppresses FSH and LH, so sperm production drops.
cards.2.p: Spermatogonia (2n) multiply by mitosis. A primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis to form four spermatids (n), which become sperm. Sperm production continues for life from puberty on.
cards.2.key: The head of a sperm holds the acrosome and the nucleus. The midpiece has mitochondria that make ATP, and the tail is at the back.
cards.2.once.soru: How many sperm form when one primary spermatocyte completes meiosis?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: Meiosis produces four cells, and all four become sperm.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: One gamete from one cell happens in oogenesis. In spermatogenesis, all four cells become sperm.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: Meiosis has two divisions and ends with four cells.
cards.3.p: The ovaries produce oocytes and secrete estrogen and progesterone. The oocyte is fertilized in the oviduct, and the embryo develops in the uterus. The vagina is the birth canal.
cards.3.key: Fertilization happens in the upper part of the oviduct, not in the uterus. The inner lining of the uterus is called the endometrium.
cards.3.once.soru: Where does fertilization usually take place?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: The sperm meets the oocyte in the upper part of the oviduct.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: The embryo develops in the uterus. Fertilization happens before that.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: The ovary releases the oocyte. Fertilization happens in the oviduct.
cards.4.p: Oogenesis begins before birth and pauses in meiosis I. After puberty, one oocyte resumes development in each cycle. Meiosis II is completed only if a sperm enters the oocyte.
cards.4.key: The secondary oocyte is released in metaphase II. The cytoplasm does not divide equally. The nutrients stay in the egg, and the polar bodies break down.
cards.5.p: The cycle lasts 28 days on average. During menstruation, the uterine lining is shed, and in the follicular phase it thickens again. At ovulation, around day 14, the oocyte is released. Then the corpus luteum forms.
cards.5.key: Cycles between 21 and 35 days are normal. The corpus luteum is also called the yellow body, and it forms from the emptied follicle.
cards.5.once.soru: Ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period. On which day is ovulation in a 32-day cycle?
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: Day 14 applies to a 28-day cycle. In a 32-day cycle, ovulation shifts later.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: The phase after ovulation always lasts about 14 days. So it is day 32 − 14 = 18.
cards.6.p: FSH makes the follicle grow, and the follicle secretes estrogen. High estrogen causes a sudden surge in LH, and ovulation occurs. Progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains the uterine lining and suppresses FSH and LH.
cards.6.key: Estrogen raising LH is positive feedback. Progesterone suppressing FSH and LH is negative feedback. Without fertilization, progesterone falls and menstruation begins.
cards.7.p: At puberty, estrogen starts the cycle. Between ages 45 and 55, the follicles run out and the cycle stops. This is called menopause. The birth control pill suppresses FSH and LH, so ovulation does not occur.
cards.7.key: The pill contains estrogen- and progesterone-like hormones and works through negative feedback. In menopause this suppression is lifted, so FSH and LH rise.
cards.7.once.soru: How does the birth control pill prevent ovulation?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: The hormones in the pill suppress the pituitary, so the follicle does not mature.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: The pill does not destroy oocytes. It only stops them from maturing.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: The pill works through hormones. It does not close the uterus.
cards.8.p: The sperm enters the oocyte in the oviduct and a zygote (2n) forms. The zygote divides by mitosis, first into a morula and then into a fluid-filled blastocyst. Around day 6-7 the blastocyst embeds in the uterus. This is called implantation.
cards.8.svg#15: about one week from oviduct to uterus
cards.8.key: Once a sperm enters, the oocyte's membrane changes and no other sperm can get in. These rapid divisions of the zygote are called cleavage.
cards.9.p: In the gastrula stage, three germ layers separate. The outer layer is the ectoderm, the middle one the mesoderm and the inner one the endoderm. The neural tube forms from the ectoderm. After week 8, the embryo is called a fetus.
cards.9.key: The ectoderm forms the skin and nerves, the mesoderm forms muscle, bone and blood, and the endoderm forms the inner linings. Differentiation happens because different genes are active in the same DNA.
cards.10.p: The amnion protects the embryo in fluid. The chorion forms the embryo's part of the placenta. In birds, the allantois stores wastes and the yolk sac provides food.
cards.10.key: In humans, the allantois helps form the umbilical cord vessels, and the yolk sac makes the first blood cells. In the umbilical cord, 2 arteries go from the baby to the placenta and 1 vein goes from the placenta to the baby.
cards.10.etk.soru: Tap the embryonic membranes and the placenta.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.0.acik: The chorion is the outermost membrane and forms the embryo's part of the placenta.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.1.acik: The amnion is a fluid-filled membrane around the embryo. It protects the embryo from bumps and drying out.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.2.acik: The embryo is the new individual that develops as the zygote divides by mitosis.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.3.acik: The umbilical cord connects the embryo to the placenta. Its vessels bring food and oxygen and carry wastes away.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.4.acik: In birds, the allantois stores wastes. In humans, it helps form the umbilical cord vessels.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.5.acik: In birds, the yolk sac provides food. In humans, it makes the first blood cells.
cards.10.etk.noktalar.6.acik: The placenta exchanges substances between mother and baby. The two bloods normally do not mix.
cards.10.once.soru: How is the baby protected from bumps in the uterus?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: The fluid inside the amnion cushions bumps.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: The baby's bones are still soft. Amniotic fluid provides the protection.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The placenta exchanges substances. Amniotic fluid absorbs the bumps.
cards.11.p: In the placenta, the mother's blood and the baby's blood do not mix. Oxygen, nutrients and some antibodies pass from mother to baby. CO<sub>2</sub> and urea pass from baby to mother. Blood cells do not cross the placenta.
cards.11.svg#8: mother's and baby's blood don't mix
cards.11.key: Alcohol, nicotine, some drugs and viruses can also cross the placenta. So the placenta is not a perfect shield.
cards.11.once.soru: Does nicotine from a pregnant woman's cigarette reach the baby?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: Nicotine, alcohol and some drugs cross the placenta.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: The placenta stops blood cells, but it cannot stop nicotine.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Nicotine reaches the baby every day throughout pregnancy.
cards.12.p: The embryo that implants in the uterus secretes the hormone hCG. hCG keeps the corpus luteum alive, so menstruation does not occur. Pregnancy tests look for this hormone. During birth, oxytocin makes the uterus contract.
cards.12.key: Contractions of the uterus cause more oxytocin to be released, and this is positive feedback. After month 3, the placenta makes the progesterone. Oxytocin also releases milk.
cards.13.p: Identical twins develop from embryos that split from a single zygote. So their genes and sex are the same. Fraternal twins form when two separate oocytes are fertilized, and they are as alike as ordinary siblings.
cards.13.key: Fraternal twins can be of different sexes. Even identical twins have different fingerprints.
cards.13.once.soru: Can a girl and a boy be identical twins?
cards.13.once.secenekler.0.neden: Identical twins have the same genes, so they also have the same sex.
cards.13.once.secenekler.1.neden: Genes determine sex. Twins with the same genes have the same sex.
cards.13.once.secenekler.2.neden: The time of birth does not change sex.
cards.14.p: Sexually transmitted infections caused by bacteria, such as chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis, are treated with antibiotics. Those caused by viruses, such as HIV, HPV and herpes, cannot be treated with antibiotics. In vitro fertilization (IVF) helps with infertility.
cards.14.svg#17: condoms reduce the risk of transmission
cards.14.key: Infertility means no pregnancy after a year of regular trying. Untreated chlamydia can block the oviducts.
cards.14.once.soru: Can HIV infection be treated with antibiotics?
cards.14.once.secenekler.0.neden: HIV is a virus. Antibiotics act only on bacteria.
cards.14.once.secenekler.2.neden: Antibiotics do not act on viruses at any stage.
cards.15.p:
• In the testis, Sertoli cells are stimulated by FSH and Leydig cells by LH.
• Oogenesis begins before birth, and meiosis II is completed at fertilization.
• High estrogen raises LH, and LH triggers ovulation.
• The zygote becomes a morula and a blastocyst, implants in the uterus, and then a gastrula forms.
• hCG maintains the corpus luteum, and oxytocin speeds up birth.
cards.15.svg#11: hormones: FSH, LH, estrogen, progesterone, hCG
quiz.0.q: At least how many primary spermatocytes must complete meiosis to produce 60 sperm?
quiz.0.e: Each primary spermatocyte forms 4 spermatids by meiosis, and these become sperm. So 60 ÷ 4 = 15 spermatocytes are needed.
quiz.1.q: Put the events from fertilization to germ layer formation in order.
quiz.1.ogeler.0: A sperm enters the secondary oocyte in the oviduct
quiz.1.ogeler.1: The nuclei fuse and a zygote (2n) forms
quiz.1.ogeler.4: The blastocyst embeds in the uterine lining (implantation)
quiz.1.ogeler.5: Three germ layers separate in the gastrula
quiz.1.e: Fertilization happens in the oviduct and a zygote forms. Dividing by mitosis, the zygote forms first a morula and then a blastocyst. The blastocyst embeds in the uterus on day 6-7. Then the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm separate in the gastrula.
quiz.2.q: Match each hormone to its job.
quiz.2.e: FSH makes the follicle grow, and the LH surge triggers ovulation. Progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains the uterine lining. hCG from the embryo keeps the corpus luteum alive. Oxytocin contracts the uterus at birth.
quiz.3.q: Which is true for twins where one is a girl and one is a boy?
quiz.3.o.2: Their genes are the same, only the sex chromosomes differ
quiz.3.o.3: One changed sex after a single zygote split
quiz.3.e: Identical twins come from the same zygote, so their genes and sex are the same. Twins of different sexes come from two separate zygotes.
quiz.3.y.0: Identical twins come from the same zygote and are always the same sex. Being born on the same day is not the test.
quiz.3.y.2: Twins of different sexes come from two separate zygotes. Their genes differ as much as ordinary siblings' genes do.
quiz.3.y.3: Sex is set at fertilization and does not change later. Different sexes show there were two separate zygotes.
A:ozet: Follow the path of sperm, run the testis with hormones, compare meiosis, find the day in the cycle and take the zygote to the uterus.
A:adimlar.0.metin: A man is having a vasectomy. In this operation, both vasa deferentia are cut and tied. Predict first, then follow the path of the sperm.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The testes keep making sperm and testosterone. Only the sperm cannot reach the way out.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.yazi: Semen forms but contains no sperm
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The fluid of semen is made by the vesicles and glands. Because the duct is cut, sperm from the epididymis cannot join this fluid.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands lie beyond the cut. So their secretions still form semen.
A:adimlar.1.metin: The pituitary sends FSH and LH to the testis. Get sperm production running at full speed.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.ipucu: Sertoli cells nourish developing sperm. Testosterone from Leydig cells keeps production going. Both are needed together.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: The two hormones worked together. Sertoli cells nourished the sperm, and testosterone from Leydig cells brought production to full speed.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Both sperm and eggs form by meiosis, but the result differs. Watch a spermatocyte divide first, then an oocyte.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: In a woman, 25 primary oocytes complete meiosis. At most how many eggs form?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Each primary oocyte forms only 1 egg. The cytoplasm does not divide equally. The nutrients stay in the egg, and the polar bodies break down.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: That is what happens with sperm, where one primary spermatocyte forms 4 sperm. In an oocyte, only one of the 4 cells is an egg.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Of the two cells formed in meiosis I, the smaller one is a polar body and cannot become an egg. In the end, each oocyte leaves 1 egg.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Ovulation is triggered by a sudden surge in the pituitary hormone LH. Slide through the days and find ovulation.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.ipucu: Look for the day when the purple LH curve shoots up. The LH peak triggers ovulation.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: The LH peak triggered ovulation. The day estrogen is highest comes just before the LH peak.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Without fertilization, the yellow body (corpus luteum) breaks down. If an embryo implants in the uterus, it secretes hCG, and pregnancy tests look for this hormone. Play both cases.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: Why does menstruation not happen when hCG is present?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The hormone that maintains the uterine lining is progesterone. hCG does this indirectly.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.yazi: hCG keeps the yellow body alive, so progesterone stays up
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: hCG prevents the yellow body from breaking down. So progesterone stays high and the lining is not shed.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: hCG raises FSH and a new follicle matures
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: No new follicle matures during pregnancy, because high progesterone suppresses FSH and LH.
A:adimlar.5.metin: The zygote divides quickly by mitosis on its way to the uterus. Predict first, then watch.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: During cleavage the number of cells rises. What happens to the embryo's total size?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: It grows at the same rate as the cell count
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Between divisions, the cells have no time to grow. So the total size does not grow.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Division does not lose material, and the outer size is kept.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Between divisions, the cells have no time to grow. With each division the cells get smaller, and the total size stays the same.
A:adimlar.6.metin: Tour the organs that develop from the germ layers. Then answer the question.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: Which layer does the inner surface of the lung's air sacs develop from?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The endoderm forms the inner linings. The linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts, the liver and the pancreas develop from the endoderm. The lung also buds off the primitive gut.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The mesoderm forms muscle, bone, the heart and blood. The muscle and vessels around the lung come from the mesoderm, but the inner surface does not.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The ectoderm forms the outer surface, that is, the epidermis and the nervous system. The lining of the air sacs is on the inside.
A:kapanis.0: Sperm are made in the testis and mature in the epididymis. Mixed with gland secretions, they form semen.
A:kapanis.1: FSH stimulates Sertoli cells, and LH stimulates Leydig cells. Leydig cells secrete testosterone.
A:kapanis.2: One spermatocyte forms 4 sperm, while one oocyte forms 1 egg. Meiosis II is completed at fertilization.
A:kapanis.3: High estrogen raises LH, and LH triggers ovulation. hCG keeps the yellow body alive.
A:kapanis.4: The zygote becomes a morula, then a blastocyst, and implants in the uterus. Then three germ layers separate in the gastrula and differentiate into organs.
